stem: The nurse reviews an adult client's body mass index (BMI) of 27 kg/m². Which interpretation is accurate?

options.A: The BMI is in the healthy-weight category
options.B: The BMI is in the overweight category
options.C: The BMI is in the obesity category
options.D: The BMI is in the underweight category

rationale: CDC defines adult overweight as BMI at least 25.0 but less than 30.0 and adult obesity as BMI at least 30.0. A BMI of 27 kg/m² therefore falls in the overweight category. BMI is a screening measure rather than a stand-alone diagnosis of an individual's health status.
educational_objective: Classify an adult BMI of 25.0 to less than 30.0 kg/m² as overweight while recognizing BMI as a screening measure rather than a complete assessment of health status.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_document_title: Data, Trends, and Maps Definitions and Sources
source_locator: Section 'Obesity and weight status' > 'Two indicators for adults 18 and older': adult obesity BMI ≥30.0; adult overweight BMI ≥25.0 but <30.0
source_claim_supported: For adults, overweight is BMI ≥25.0 but <30.0 and obesity is BMI ≥30.0; therefore BMI 27 kg/m² is classified as overweight.
blueprint_locator: Basic Care and Comfort, Nutrition and Oral Hydration, printed p.37 / PDF p.40: 'Apply knowledge of mathematics to client nutrition (e.g., body mass index)'
blueprint_topic: Basic Care and Comfort — Nutrition and Oral Hydration / body mass index
correction_summary: Specified that the client is an adult so pediatric percentile criteria cannot apply; replaced the older generic CDC BMI citation with a current CDC 2026 definition and exact locator; corrected the NCLEX blueprint from Reduction of Risk Potential to Basic Care and Comfort because the 2026 Test Plan explicitly places body mass index under Nutrition and Oral Hydration.
audit_findings: B is directly supported by the current CDC adult BMI definition. A, C, and D fall outside the verified adult threshold containing BMI 27. The adult qualifier removes age-dependent ambiguity, and the rationale avoids treating BMI as a complete diagnosis. No second answer, cueing, unsupported precision, or unresolved conflict remains.
